items.text: Whether you've reached work or study burnout, you're going through relationship dramas, or you just feel weighed down by life in general, stress is something that's difficult to avoid.

level1.label: 让步状语从句
level1.text: Whether you've reached work or study burnout, you're going through relationship dramas, or you just feel weighed down by life in general

items.text: If only there were an easy and free way to alleviate it.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: an easy and free way to alleviate it

items.text: Luckily, there is!
Breathwork.
Breathing is the first and last thing we do on this planet, and it's the simplest way we can alleviate stress and anxiety both immediately and long-term, when done properly.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the first and last thing we do on this planet

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the simplest way we can alleviate stress and anxiety both immediately and long-term

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: we can alleviate stress and anxiety both immediately and long-term

items.text: So, how can we reap the benefits?
It's about slowing down.
"We all tend to hyperventilate, breathing too fast and not very effectively," says David Spiegel, professor of psychiatry and behavioural sciences at Stanford University in the US.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: breathing too fast and not very effectively

level1.label: 同位语
level1.text: professor of psychiatry and behavioural sciences at Stanford University in the US

items.text: One way to make our breathing more intentional is a technique called 'cyclic sighing', with a focus on prolonged exhalation.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: One way to make our breathing more intentional

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: to make our breathing more intentional

items.text: Begin with a deep inhale through your nose.
Just when you think you're done, take a short, sharp breath to fully fill the lungs.
Then, let out a slow and extended sigh to completely empty your lungs.
A 2023 study published in PubMed by Spiegel and colleagues found that just five minutes a day of cyclic sighing improved mood and lowered anxiety.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: A 2023 study published in PubMed by Spiegel and colleagues

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that just five minutes a day of cyclic sighing improved mood and lowered anxiety

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: published in PubMed by Spiegel and colleagues

items.text: For a more advanced method, try 'coherent breathing'.
To do this, you want to find a comfortable position, with one hand on your belly, and the other on your chest.
Inhale through your nose for about six seconds, making the hand on your belly rise by engaging your diaphragm.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: making the hand on your belly rise by engaging your diaphragm

items.text: Then exhale for the same duration.
The key is to keep your breath smooth and continuous.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: to keep your breath smooth and continuous

items.text: "Imagine your breath as a slow tide coming in and going out," says Guy Fincham, who leads a breathwork research lab at Brighton and Sussex Medical School in the UK.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: Guy Fincham, who leads a breathwork research lab at Brighton and Sussex Medical School in the UK

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: who leads a breathwork research lab at Brighton and Sussex Medical School in the UK

items.text: The A52 breath method is similar, except at the end of the exhalation, you hold your breath for a couple of seconds before breathing in again.

Slowing down our breathing works because it relaxes the sympathetic nervous system, which is responsible for the 'fight-or-flight' response and activates the parasympathetic nervous system, responsible for the body's 'rest-and-digest' functions.

level1.label: 原因状语从句

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: which is responsible for the 'fight-or-flight' response and activates the parasympathetic nervous system

items.text: This calms the body.
So, whenever you start to feel overwhelmed, remember that you have this easy and instant stress-reliever in your toolkit.
